processing_steps.atmosphere: 10^-5 mbar pressure, backfilled with argon gas atmosphere
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Remelted 5-6 times without breaking vacuum for better elemental intermixing (AM500-Edmund Buhler GmbH, Germany)
Homogenization performed in a muffle furnace
Nine passes in a 75-ton rolling mill; finish rolling temperature 900 °C
Air-cooled HR sheet was sectioned into smaller pieces; CR further thins B2 stringer bands and pancakes γ

structures.overall_structure: Banded two-phase microstructure: thinner, more closely spaced B2 stringer bands alternating with pancaked/deformed γ matrix

phases_present.morphology: thin, elongated, more closely spaced deformed stringer bands

grain_structure.texture: RD-aligned lamellar/banded structure; γ pancaked along prior RD

precipitates.distribution: Precipitated IG-B2 undergoes shape deformation during CR

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: EBSD phase and KAM maps show co-deformation of B2 stringer bands and γ during CR, with higher local misorientation (strain) in the softer γ bands than in the B2 stringer bands

interfaces.slip_behavior: co-deformation of γ and B2 stringer bands during cold rolling; strain concentrates preferentially in softer γ
interfaces.phase_evolution: CR further thins B2 stringer bands, pancakes γ, and shape-deforms precipitated IG-B2

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: rolling direction (RD); gauge length 12.5 mm, gauge width 3 mm, thickness 2 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: 100 kN Instron 5982 with 10 mm gauge extensometer

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve for CR shown in Figure 5a; CR peaks at or just above 1500 MPa below 2% strain and then drops steeply (strongest and least ductile condition)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 3% nital etch; ground and polished (emery paper, cloth polishing with SiC abrasive)
characterization_methods.purpose: reveal CR microstructure: thinner, more closely spaced B2 stringer bands and pancaked γ
characterization_methods.key_findings: CR shows the same lamellar architecture as HR but with thinner, denser B2 stringer bands and flattened/pancaked γ

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FESEM (Apreo S) with routine EBSD setup
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electropolished in 10% perchloric acid 90% acetic acid solution at 20 V and 5 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: EBSD phase map and KAM map of the CR condition
characterization_methods.key_findings: Banded two-phase structure of deformed B2 stringer bands and deformed γ; higher local misorientation (strain) in γ than in B2 stringer bands

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: 100 kN Instron 5982 with 10 mm gauge extensometer
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, ASTM E8, RD, gauge length 12.5 mm, gauge width 3 mm, thickness 2 mm, crosshead velocity 1 mm/min
characterization_methods.purpose: measure mechanical properties of the CR sheet
characterization_methods.key_findings: CR is the strongest (peak at or just above 1500 MPa) and least ductile (fracture below ~2% strain); toughness 0.11 kJ/mol (15.2 J/cm^3)

unmapped_findings: The CR sample (cold-rolled sheet, standard process) is the strongest (peak at or just above 1500 MPa) but least ductile (fracture below ~2% strain) among the HR/CR/annealed conditions; CR reduces ductility even further relative to HR (~6.8% ductility).
